Check Optional Software for Bayesian Scale Models

Source: R/bayes_scale_setup.R
check_bayes_setup.Rd

Check whether the R packages that a multiScale_bayes() computation method needs can be loaded and meet the package's minimum versions. Nothing is installed, no model is fitted, and neither the compiler nor sampling performance is tested.

Usage

check_bayes_setup(
  method = c("sample", "laplace", "marginal", "prepare", "slice"),
  correction = c("none", "importance"),
  cores = 1L
)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_bayes_setup'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

method

Computation method to check, as in multiScale_bayes(). "sample" (default, NUTS) needs RTMB, tmbstan, rstan, and posterior. "laplace" and "marginal" need RTMB. "slice" and "prepare" need no optional packages to run in one process. Slice chain diagnostics need posterior (version 1.6.0 or later).

correction

"none" (default) or "importance". Importance correction applies only to method = "marginal" and also needs posterior.

cores

Requested number of worker processes; default 1. A value greater than one also checks processx, which parallel fits need. It has no effect for "prepare", which always uses one process.

x

A multiScaleR_bayes_setup object from check_bayes_setup().

...

Not used. Supplying any further argument is an error.

Value

An object of class multiScaleR_bayes_setup, a list with these elements.

  • method, correction: the settings checked.

  • ready: TRUE when every listed package loads and meets its minimum version.

  • packages: a data frame with one row per package and columns package, minimum (the minimum version, or NA when any version works), installed version, loadable, meets_version, passed, and a diagnostic message that says what to install or update.

  • notes: what the check does and does not cover.

Printing the object lists the packages and the notes, and returns it invisibly. A passed check does not certify a working compiler, successful sampling, convergence, or adequate memory. Fit a small model next.

Details

Preparation (method = "prepare") validates your data and formulas before you install any sampling software. Installing the NUTS packages from source can require a C++ compiler, which on Windows comes with Rtools. vignette("v13-bayesian-scales", package = "multiScaleR") covers installation, and vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") compares the methods.

See also

multiScale_bayes()

Examples

check_bayes_setup(method = "prepare")  # always ready: nothing to install
#> Bayesian package setup: prepare 
#> Package checks passed.
#> Preparation needs no optional Bayesian packages.
#> Checks R packages only; does not install software or run a model.
#> Compiler configuration, memory and sampling diagnostics require a separate small fit. 

# Packages for slice sampling on two workers. `ready` is FALSE when
# processx is missing. The message column says what to install.
setup <- check_bayes_setup(method = "slice", cores = 2)
setup$ready
#> [1] TRUE
setup$packages[c("package", "loadable", "passed")]
#>    package loadable passed
#> 1 processx     TRUE   TRUE
